pr_body:
As noted in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/78295#issuecomment-1606067045, the editor wasn't using null icon cache correctly. This PR makes the `get_script_icon()` return null early if the cache contains null and also moves some script-related logic to this method, so more code is cached.

Fixes #78295
It's noticeably faster, but still quite slow. I only tested debug build though.
pr_comments:
Tested locally, it works. When at the bottom of the scene tree dock in the MRP, it now takes 1 second to duplicate a node with a debug build as opposed to 5 seconds. Scrolling is still slower the lower you get in the scene tree dock though.

Script icons appear successfully in add-ons such as [Cyclops](https://github.com/blackears/cyclopsLevelBuilder).

### Profiling of a debug build with `master`

![Screenshot_20230626_102515](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/180032/351b794f-09dc-4111-9687-fa198b5ece6c)

It's interesting to see `Vector2i::operator Vector2()` taking so much time in `TreeItem::get_minimum_size()`. Is there a way to avoid those conversions?

As I read it, it's `Vector2i::operator Vector2` in the flame graph, so it should actually be a conversion from `Vector2i` to `Vector2`, which doesn't seem to be the one you changed. But from a quick look I don't see where a `Vector2i` is converted to a `Vector2`.

Aside from this one maybe, which is called from `get_minimum_size()` (maybe it's inlined and doesn't appear in the flame graph?):
```cpp
Size2 Tree::_get_cell_icon_size(const TreeItem::Cell &p_cell) const {
	Size2i icon_size = p_cell.get_icon_size(); // Size2 -> Size2i
```

Still, if this kind of simple conversion is so costly, that's definitely something worth looking into in a separate issue as it would have big consequences on the whole engine and editor code.

*Edit:* Oh I misread, your change to `cached_minimum_size` should indeed prevent a conversion from `Size2i` to `Size2` every single time `get_minimum_size()` is called. That does seem worth doing. Maybe @Calinou can re-run the perf check with that change.

issue_context.title: Very noticeable performance issues when adding nodes to a scene that contains many scripted nodes (editor)
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot 4.1-beta2

### System information

Manjaro Gnome, Intel Core i7-11800H

### Issue description

On a relatively modern laptop (Intel Core i7-11800H), in a scene with many scripted nodes (total of 900+ with roughly half of them scripted), adding or duplicating a node freezes the editor for several seconds. Godot 4.0.2 handles such scenes much better!

Here is a flame graph captured while repeatedly duplicating simple Marker2D nodes with Ctrl+D in a complicated scene:
![Screenshot from 2023-06-15 23-54-38](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2766569/d0019f17-9b82-4a26-9b47-71fa7a3bef3a)

Performance data file to use with hotspot v1.4.1 (relevant data starts at the 75-second mark and lasts about 20+ seconds):
[perf.data.perfparser.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11763700/perf.data.perfparser.zip)



### Steps to reproduce

1) Add 1000 nodes with a script attached.
2) Duplicate a node and witness lags.

Also affects scrolling the scene tree dock.

### Minimal reproduction project

[add_node_lags_repro.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11763731/add_node_lags_repro.zip)
comments:
If you can [compile the engine from source](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/development/compiling/index.html), you could look into [bisecting the regression](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/community/contributing/bisecting_regressions.html) to greatly speed up troubleshooting.

Given the presence of `EditorNode::_get_class_or_script_icon()`, I'm guessing this has to do with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/75472. I still recommend bisecting to check whether this is actually the case though.

Sounds similar to #60127
Script icons are already cached, but `_get_class_or_script_icon()` doesn't fully utilize the cache probably.

`EditorData` is responsible for caching all the information about scripts, and from the chart in the OP I can see that its methods get hit, but then continue into the GDScript module. Which means there were no cache entries for the scripts that it tried to check.

Also keep in mind that `EditorNode::_get_class_or_script_icon` is called for any type, including built-in types which are fetched directly from the theme. So it's going to be called a lot regardless of the scripted classes. But I don't believe that the changes made to it significantly modify the logic compared to 4.0.x.

Just to be clear, the simple reproduction project performs much faster in 4.0.2. There are no noticeable lags. Removing scripts from the nodes also reduces lags by a big margin.
EDIT: will try to bisect the issue today.

I've noticed this in my game too. Whenever I move a 3D object in the editor, it freezes for about a second. It definitely seems related to this script issue, as I was able to recreate the issue in a new scene with lots of duplicated nodes. The issue persisted until I finally tried removing the attached scripts, and then suddenly the issue went away.

Just chiming in to say that I experience this with opening/switching to any large-ish scenes, which takes about 10 seconds in 4.1 and was nearly instant in 4.0. So I've stuck with 4.0.3. The issues for me started with 4.1-dev4.
Will this be solved for the 4.1 release?

I think the problem is here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3710f069293f2fde8afe33fea898c4b36fa5e943/editor/editor_data.cpp#L1117
Before #75472 the icon could get cached as null and the script wouldn't be re-parsed, but that's not true anymore.

EDIT:
Fixing this is not enough.
I can confirm that #78670 improves performance. It is still worse than in version 4.0.2; however, the performance improvements are considerable and position it closer to 4.0.2 than beta 3.
4.1-rc1 has eliminated the slowdown for me! :)

review_comments:
Problem with caching this is that adding icons to an existing class would require an editor restart. Though I guess changing an icon already requires an editor restart. We need a way to invalidate this cache. I guess this could be fine for now.

Would you mind adding a TODO comment around here somewhere pointing that limitation out and mentioning that we need to invalidate the cache when relevant?
Currently the cache is cleared when closing a scene tab.

Uh-huh. Well that explains why things are so slow. We try to rely on this cache everywhere in the editor, but the moment any scene is closed, we just flush all of it. That's not great. I now realize that I have touched this code, but missed the implication of it.

> Before https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/75472 the icon could get cached as null and the script wouldn't be re-parsed, but that's not true anymore.

Well, this line still exists.

So if we are to go ahead with this, I would add a comment next to the edited line that removes the validity check mentioning that we are being purposefully eager and ignoring invalid cache for the sake of performance. Probably a FIXME comment that should be.

The line existed but the null was unused.
Also not sure what you mean by FIXME, this is intended behavior. If the script does not provide icon, there is no reason to parse it again.

Script may be changed after we record this into cache. So if we don't check for validity, an editor restart would be required for the icon to be updated. That's why I put the check there.

Edit: That was assumption about the cache at least. It seems that this is not how it works though, and I've missed that it's cleared when scene tabs are closed.

> The line existed but the null was unused.

Not sure what you mean by that.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3710f069293f2fde8afe33fea898c4b36fa5e943/editor/editor_data.cpp#L1117
This basically means that the cache was used only when the icon was valid.
